subject: Model fit review + prompt collection request (Acme Search)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Ellis Zhao <ellis@acme-search.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Model fit review + prompt collection request (Acme Search)

Hi Ellis — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: search-result summarization and relevance re-ranking for enterprise documents.
- Scale: ~5k active queries/day initially, bursty peaks up to ~2k q/hr.
- SLOs: target median latency <200ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), batch throughput for nightly re-rank.
- Data sensitivity: some prompts may contain user PII and internal document snippets — customer expects controls around redaction and auditability.

Model-fit hypothesis
- Recommendation to evaluate two families in parallel: a midsize instruction-tuned family for cost-sensitive flows and a larger context-sensitive family for quality-critical re-rank. Early candidates: 
  * Redwood-13B-instruct (quantized q4) — good balance of latency/cost and instruction-following.
  * Mistral-7B-instruct (high instruction-quality for short-context prompts) — cost-efficient for high QPS.

What we need from you
1) Prompt set: a CSV with representative query prompts (include expected/desired output where possible). We typically ask for 200–500 items; a first batch of ~100 is fine to get an initial fit. Please put the file in the shared folder below or reply with a sample in-line.
2) Edge-case notes: list of ~10 known failure modes (examples: overly long legal snippets, proprietary tokens, PII-heavy examples, multilingual queries). Mark which are high-priority.
3) Redaction / compliance constraints: call out any regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR requirements) and examples of data you cannot send even for evaluation.

Attachments & links
- I attached a short model-recs PDF with expected latency/cost ballparks. (redwood_model-recs.pdf)
- Upload prompts here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeSharedPromptBucket
- Benchmark/eval template we’ll use: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-search-eval-2026

Proposed timeline
- You upload an initial prompt batch by EOD Friday (Feb 19).
- We run an initial fit/eval and share results within 3 business days.
- Follow-up call to review model-fit and canary plan week of Feb 23.

Notes on privacy/redaction (short)
- If prompts contain PII, please replace with placeholders (e.g., [CUSTOMER_NAME], [EMAIL]) prior to upload unless you confirm we may store raw test data under an agreed NDA/audit trail. We’ll provide a redaction checklist if helpful.

Next step: can I confirm you’ll drop a CSV in the Drive and I’ll book a 30-min review for Feb 23?

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aomi@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Sample prompts (raw):
1) "Summarize the litigation notes for Acme v. Zeta showing only actions and dates."
2) "Given the user search: "API rate limiting errors", return the top 3 KB articles and a 2-sentence summary for each."
3) "Rewrite this customer note to remove identifying info and convert into a 3-bullet support summary:

---"

Edge-case concerns:
- We have PHI in a small subset of documents (medical metadata attached to some support tickets). We cannot send raw PHI outside our VPC.
- Proprietary tokens: some of our documents include internal product codenames that must stay obfuscated during eval.

Question: what do you recommend as an appropriate redaction approach so our legal team is comfortable? Also can you provide a rough per-1k-token cost estimate for the Redwood-13B-instruct quantized option?

—

Subject: Re: Model fit review + prompt collection request (Acme Search)

Thanks Ellis — that's perfect. Short answers and next actions below.

Redaction guidance (recommended, concise)
- Client-side pseudonymization: replace direct identifiers with deterministic placeholders prior to upload (e.g., [USER_12345], [EMAIL_1]). Keep a local mapping in your environment only.
- For PHI: do not upload raw PHI to hosted evals. Two options:
  1) Run the initial eval in your VPC/private deployment (we can spin a short-lived private job) so no raw PHI leaves your environment.
  2) If you share synthetic variants, replace PHI with placeholders and mark those prompts as "synthetic-PHI" in the CSV.
- For proprietary tokens: replace with stable tokens like [PRODUCT_X]; include a separate doc mapping tokens to high-level categories (not the real names) so evaluators can interpret without exposure.

Cost ballpark (Redwood-13B-instruct, quantized q4)
- Rough: $0.60–$1.20 per 1k tokens for interactive evals (depends on batching and sequence lengths). We’ll provide a more precise estimate after we see your prompt length distribution.

Attachments
- I attached the redaction checklist (pii-redaction-checklist.md) and a short PDF with candidate model latency/costs (redwood_model-recs.pdf).

Proposed next steps
1) You upload a CSV (first batch 100 prompts) to the Drive by Thu Feb 19. Flag up to 10 edge cases in a separate column.
2) Rishi will run a quick model-fit run and provide a results doc (~3 business days).
3) Book a 30-min review on Feb 23 to go over results and next steps (canary plan/rollout).

I'll draft the calendar invite; Rishi — can you confirm availability Feb 23 for a 30-min slot?

Thanks — Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman

Rishi / Marissa — internal action items from the Acme thread (summary):

Context: Acme (DEAL-2026-ACME-009) will upload an initial 100-prompt CSV to our shared Drive by Feb 19. They flagged PHI and proprietary tokens. They prefer not to send raw PHI to hosted evals.

Ask / assignments:
- Rishi: run a 2-model quick-fit using Redwood-13B-instruct-q4 and Mistral-7B-instruct on the incoming CSV. Focus metrics: ROUGE-L for summarization prompts, top-3 precision for KB retrieval prompts, and a qualitative checklist for hallucination. Produce a short results doc within 3 business days of upload. Use private ephemeral job if Acme requests VPC-hosted eval.
- Marissa: prepare the ingestion template (CSV with columns: id, prompt_raw, prompt_redacted, expected_output, edge_case_flag, priority). Add a column for "redaction_notes" and include the pii-redaction-checklist.md as a sample.
- Naomi: I’ll own scheduling the Feb 23 review and communicating cost ballpark info to the customer.

Dependencies / risks:
- If they insist on raw-PHI being evaluated in our hosted environment, Legal will need to sign off. Plan B is run the eval inside their VPC.
- Watch for long-context prompts (>2k tokens) — may require a different model/config.

Let’s sync 30 minutes Monday (Feb 22) to confirm slots and the canary deployment steps (if results look good).

—
Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
